correctness.rationale: For arbitrary n>=4, every proper root-polytope face is canonically a complete bipartite root face F_(A,B), of cone dimension |A|+|B|-1 with |A||B| rays. Star-tree incidence rays are unimodular, whereas all nonsimplicial cones (both sides at least two) contain a minimal 2-by-2 square. Therefore the reduced singular locus has precisely 6 binomial(n,4) torus-orbit-closure components. The quotient star fan is the sign-orthant fan of rank n-4, so each component is a product of projective lines. The saturated rank-three square cone has dual affine ring k[u,v,s,t]/(uv-st), giving its generic transverse completion. The polar lattice polytope is max(h)-min(h)<=1; its square-cone face is a unit (n-4)-cube, giving O(1,...,1) and degree (n-4)!. P has only origin and roots as lattice points, so the toric Fano variety is terminal Gorenstein. All assertions are integral and characteristic-free. Included standalone checker executed successfully through n=7; finite tests are not offered as all-n proofs.

originality.rationale: The prior 2008 paper already proves the root-polytope facet products of simplices and the first n=4 root example, Higashitani proves the graph-Fano construction and smoothness tests, and the 2021 directed-graph paper identifies four-cycle obstructions to codimension-three Q-factoriality. These established facts are explicitly separated from the proposed complete all-index classification of irreducible singular orbit closures as products of P1, the uniform generic conifold, and their restricted -K degrees. The inspected source sections do not give the joint theorem. Equivalent implicit consequences in broader toric literature are an acknowledged residual risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent theorem may be formulated as the singular strata of the type-A permutohedral/root toric Fano variety rather than as a symmetric-edge polytope theorem.

The component count alone is close to a straightforward consequence of classical face products; originality and value rest on the combined complete geometric classification, transverse algebra and polarization.

value.rationale: The infinite complete-graph type-A root family is a canonical, naturally occurring terminal toric Fano example. A complete pure-codimension-three singular-support classification, exact abstract component geometry, characteristic-free transverse conifold model, and anticanonical degree are motivated invariants relevant to toric singularity and intersection geometry. Prior codimension-three non-Q-factorial criteria do not by themselves determine these precise geometric facts. The theorem avoids arbitrary finite slicing and does not claim a new face f-vector.
